key_insight: Higher cold-spray pressure raises copper particle velocity above the bonding threshold, improving inter-particle bonding and ductility while preserving good conductivity.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies a practical pressure window for producing copper CSAM parts with a better balance of mechanical performance and electrical conductivity for functional components.
method: Cold-sprayed copper at 30, 40, 50, and 60 bar using a LightSPEE3D system.
Characterised deposits by XRD, SEM, hardness, eddy current conductivity, and tensile testing.
Compared microstructure and property changes against spray pressure-driven particle velocity changes.
evidence_signal: Data showed progressive crystallite refinement, higher dislocation density, increased conductivity, lower hardness, and a clear strength-to-ductility transition at higher pressures.
watch_item: Higher-pressure settings may improve ductility and bonding, but process optimisation is needed to avoid over-softening from recovery/recrystallisation or pressure-specific variability.
paper_title: Optimising Cold Spray Additive Manufacturing: Pressure-driven enhancement of mechanical performance in copper deposits
